elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 6.1 now reads only "HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the 'Deerskin' brand for a self-contained web site..."; the Company covenant ("the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site ... with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products") is deleted, and no other field-of-use or territory restriction binds the Company. Deterministic check "no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains" is ok.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction on the Company survives after deletion of the 6.1 covenant, so there is no scope to narrow to a named competing product.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the Company covenant removed, nothing binds the Company either during or after the term (Section 4.1's auto-renewing one-year term no longer carries any Customer covenant).

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no surviving Customer restriction to which a duration cap could attach.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no prohibition on the Company remains, so its internal development is unrestricted without needing an express carve-out; Section 6.2's closeout-site right is retained.
Condition does not apply: the deleted covenant was the only bar on Company activity, so acquisitions are unconstrained.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative text removes the Company's non-compete/field-of-use covenant entirely, including the open-ended "products substantially similar" and "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" language that failed the fallback on scope.
Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because no restriction on the Customer survives; nothing further is required to narrow scope, term, duration, or carve-outs.

Minimal: the edit is a single targeted deletion of the Customer covenant (and the now-purposeless "Except as provided in Section 6.2" lead-in). It retains HDI's exclusive "Deerskin" brand right, Section 6.2's closeout-site right, and Section 4.1's term/termination mechanics unchanged, and adds no survival, expense, or procedural boilerplate.

Preserves intent: Section 6.2 stands on its own as an affirmative Company right, so deleting the "Except as provided in Section 6.2" carve-in leaves no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence; Section 4.1's renewal mechanics and HDI's exclusivity remain internally consistent.

Comment complies with tone and playbook practice: it states what was deleted, why we cannot restrict our business, and offers the narrowed fallback (named competing product, term only, \u226412 months, internal development and acquisition carve-outs) without lecturing.
